tasks.short: Assess a patient's risk of harm to self or others.

steps.what: Read the referral about harm to self
Open prior risk entries in the clinical record
Study earlier assessments in the case history
Interview the patient about harm to others
Draft the risk formulation from the interview

loop.input: The spoken risk assessment from the interview and the case history notes already opened.
loop.output: A risk formulation draft. It is wording only. It is not a harm score and not a diagnosis.
loop.check: The draft has a formulation section and at least one quoted line from the interview. The check does not judge harm.
loop.stop: The draft is written. The loop does not wait for the psychologist. If the interview was not recorded, the loop does not run.
loop.why_not_simpler: The formulation is free text. A stored form has no place for causes, plan, and means. Plain code cannot write that prose. The loop only drafts.

steps.what: Check formulation meaning against spoken assessments
Commit the accepted risk formulation to the record

tasks.design: The clinical psychologist interviews the patient and decides the risk of harm. A bounded loop in the {OTHER} clinical record drafts formulation wording from that interview and the case history, then stops. The psychologist checks the meaning and only then commits that accepted version. The draft is not a harm score.
tasks.previous_blocker: The formulation is free text about this patient, and a wrong harm judgement can injure someone, so it could not be a stored calculation.
tasks.enabler_now: Speech can be turned into a documentation draft inside the record the clinic already uses. The psychologist still decides harm.
tasks.still_hard: The psychologist must hear the patient and own the harm decision. A recording needs consent, and the note is health data.
tasks.human_edge: Only the psychologist can judge intent, means, and immediacy with this patient.
tasks.altitude: The harm decision stays with the clinical psychologist. Less time goes to typing the first formulation. Decision rights do not move.

reach.task: Decide which harm signs belong in the formulation and which belong in the neuro exam
reach.learn: Which phrases in the formulation a neuro exam can cite without repeating the interview

evidence.claim: Speech-driven reporting drafts clinical documentation from the clinician's own speech. It does not assess risk of harm.
One psychiatry clinic tried ambient voice notes as a documentation assistant. This design does not use that study's minutes as a saving.
The psychologist stays accountable for an AI-drafted note.
A risk formulation is free text. A stored form does not hold causes, plan, and means. A model must not score harm or infer emotion. Model knowledge.

assumptions: Means priors sum to 99.9 and are scaled to 100. Largest remainder gives screens 6, a one-point grid prior, mail 2, documents 23, and meetings 68. The grid point is folded into documents because the formulation is prose in the {OTHER} record. Document time is 16 to study, 4 to draft, 2 to check, and 2 to commit. That split is a design choice, not a measured study.

The draft reads the spoken risk assessment produced in the interview and the case history opened on screen. If the interview is not recorded, the draft does not run and the psychologist writes the formulation by hand.
The loop stops when the draft is written. It does not wait for a person. The check names accepted risk formulation v1. The commit does not edit that version. A later edit voids the check.
The formulation draft is only the harm wording. It is not the session note counted on the documentation task. The interview stays at full time.
No focal upkeep is added. Exceptions sit inside the remaining check. Record runtime earns no labour saving.
unknowns: Whether this clinic already records the risk interview.
Whether a works council would treat that recording as a personnel system. The digest names the Netherlands for staff surveys and selection tools, not for this clinical interview.
Whether past harm entries are stored as text in the {OTHER} record.
research_questions: Which formulation headings does this clinical record already require?

already_counted.description: Checking formulation meaning against the spoken assessment is already the full time of that check.

incremental.description: Keeping the formulation section available in the clinical record module.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low is 0 when the interview is not recorded and the psychologist writes the formulation by hand. High is 2 when a recording exists for only some encounters, so only part of the formulation typing is avoided. The interview, the harm decision, and the check stay at full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Write session notes, progress notes, recommendations, and treatment plans.

steps.what: Open the prior treatment plan in the record
Read the last progress notes and recommendations
Attend the session and mark points for notes
Draft session notes and the treatment plan update

loop.input: Marked points from this session, the prior treatment plan, and the last progress notes.
loop.output: A draft of the session notes and the treatment plan update.
loop.check: Each required note heading has a line, and each line quotes a marked point from the session. The check does not judge treatment.
loop.stop: The draft is written. The loop does not wait for the psychologist. If the session was not recorded, the loop does not run.
loop.why_not_simpler: Session notes, progress notes, recommendations, and the treatment plan update are prose. A stored form cannot write them. The loop only drafts.

steps.what: Check the notes against the session and the plan
Commit accepted notes and the plan to the record
Send the accepted recommendations to the physician

tasks.design: The clinical psychologist attends the session and marks the points that belong in the notes. A bounded loop in the {OTHER} record drafts the session notes and the treatment plan update from those points, then stops. The psychologist checks that draft against the session, commits the accepted version, and sends those recommendations to the physician by {EMAIL} without editing them.
tasks.previous_blocker: The four note types are different prose artefacts written after the session, and the psychologist remains accountable for every line.
tasks.enabler_now: A documentation draft can be made from speech the psychologist already gathers in the session. The record the clinic uses can hold the accepted note.
tasks.still_hard: The psychologist must still compare the draft with what the patient said. Consent to record, and health-data access, stay in the way.
tasks.human_edge: Only the psychologist knows which remark in the session changes the treatment plan.
tasks.altitude: Sessions stay with the clinical psychologist. Typing the first note takes less time. The decision about what the note says does not move.

reach.task: Write a classroom observation the clinic note can cite
reach.learn: How the observation is worded so the clinic note does not repeat the session

evidence.claim: Speech-driven reporting drafts clinical documentation from the clinician's own speech.
One psychiatry clinic tried ambient voice notes as a documentation assistant. This design does not use that study's minutes as a saving.
The psychologist stays accountable for an AI-drafted note.
Session notes, progress notes, recommendations, and treatment plans are different prose artefacts written after the session. Model knowledge.

assumptions: Means priors sum to 100.1 and are scaled to 100. Largest remainder gives screens 30, a one-point grid prior, mail 3, documents 42, and meetings 24. The grid point is folded into documents because the notes are prose. Screens are 8 to open the plan and 22 to draft. Documents are 10 to read, 18 to check, and 15 to commit. Mail is the physician send. That split is a design choice, not a measured study.

The draft reads marked session points produced while the psychologist attends the session, plus the prior treatment plan and the last progress notes. If the session is not recorded, the draft does not run and the psychologist types the notes by hand.

The loop stops when the draft is written. It does not wait for a person. The check names accepted session record v1. The commit and the physician send do not edit that version. A later edit voids the check.
The physician is treated as outside the clinic, so the send leaves the organisation. The note draft does not include the harm formulation counted on the risk task. Attendance stays at full time.
No focal upkeep is added. Exceptions sit inside the remaining check. Record runtime earns no labour saving.
unknowns: Whether this clinic already records sessions.
Whether the physician who receives the recommendations sits outside the organisation.
Which of the four note types this record already stores as separate documents.
research_questions: Which note headings does this clinical record already require?

already_counted.description: Checking the notes against the session and the plan is already the full time of that check.

incremental.description: Keeping the four note headings available in the clinical record module.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low is 0 when the session is not recorded and the psychologist types the notes by hand. High is 12 when about half of sessions have a usable recording and the treatment plan update is still retyped often. Attendance, reading, the check, the commit, and the physician send stay at full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Diagnose disorders from interviews, tests, records, and reference materials.

steps.what: Open test forms and earlier diagnostic records
Read the referral that asks for a diagnosis
Compute the scaled score from stored test items
Study prior interviews, tests, and reference materials
Interview the client to diagnose disorders

tasks.design: The clinical psychologist opens the test form in the {OTHER} record and reads the referral and the reference materials in {DOCS}. The test module computes one scaled score from stored item responses and the publisher norm table. The psychologist studies that score and then interviews the client to diagnose the disorder. The score is not a diagnosis.
tasks.previous_blocker: Naming a disorder depends on this client, and a wrong diagnosis can change treatment. Only the arithmetic of a stored test was ever a calculation.
tasks.enabler_now: Where item responses are already fields on the test form, the test module the clinic uses can apply the norm table without new code.
tasks.still_hard: The diagnosis stays a judgement in the interview. Test results are health data, and the clinic may not be licensed to store every norm table.
tasks.human_edge: Only the psychologist can decide which disorder fits this client after the interview.
tasks.altitude: The diagnosis stays with the clinical psychologist. The only time removed is totalling stored items. Decision rights do not move.

reach.task: Choose the next test after a scaled score
reach.learn: When a scaled score changes the differential the clinic interview is testing

evidence.claim: A scaled score from stored item responses and a publisher norm table is arithmetic. Naming the disorder is not. Model knowledge.

assumptions: Means priors sum to 100. Largest remainder gives screens 6, a one-point grid prior, mail 3, documents 29, and meetings 61. The grid point is this task's scaled-score step on the {OTHER} test module. It is not a separate grid and it is not reused from another task.

The score step reads item responses stored as fields on the test form opened in the first step, plus the norm table in the test module. Its output is one scaled score, not a disorder. If responses are not stored fields, the psychologist totals them while studying the file and the score step does not run.
The diagnosis is made in the interview. This task does not commit a separate report, so there is no approval. Writing the diagnosis into a note or a report belongs to those tasks.
No focal upkeep is added. Loading the norm table is system time, not the psychologist's week. If the psychologist must load it, that time is not in this estimate.
Giving the test is treated as already done, because the task uses tests already obtained. That sitting is not given a new baseline here.
unknowns: Whether item responses are stored fields or only a total written in prose.
Which publisher norm table the clinic is licensed to keep in the test module.
Whether the psychologist, rather than an administrator, must load that norm table.
research_questions: Which norm tables may this clinic store in the test module?

incremental.description: Loading a licensed norm table into the test module. This is not the psychologist's week.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low is 0 when item responses are not stored fields and the psychologist totals them by hand while studying the file. High is 1 when responses are stored and the arithmetic runs. The interview and the diagnosis stay at full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Write client reports and keep the required paperwork.

steps.what: Open the chart notes and stored test scores
Read the referral question and report headings
Agree the report facts with the client in person
Draft client reports from the notes and scores

loop.input: Agreed facts from the client meeting, chart notes, stored test scores, and the report headings.
loop.output: A client report draft. Findings are quoted from the notes. Scores are copied, not interpreted.
loop.check: Each report heading has a quoted line from a chart note or a stored score. The check does not judge the findings.
loop.stop: The draft is written. The loop does not wait for the psychologist. If the notes were not stored, the loop does not run.
loop.why_not_simpler: The report is prose around the psychologist's own notes. Plain code can copy a stored score but cannot write the findings. The loop only drafts.

steps.what: Check findings, limits, and the required paperwork
Commit the accepted report with the required paperwork
Send the accepted report to the external referrer

tasks.design: The clinical psychologist agrees the facts with the client, then a bounded loop in the {OTHER} record drafts the report from the chart notes, the stored scores, and the headings in {DOCS}. The loop stops when the draft is written. The psychologist checks the findings and the required paperwork, commits that accepted version, and sends it to the referrer by {EMAIL} without editing it.
tasks.previous_blocker: Findings and limits are a judgement, and a report that leaves the clinic can be relied on by a referrer, a court, or an insurer.
tasks.enabler_now: The notes and scores are already in the clinical record, so a documentation draft can quote them. The psychologist still checks every finding.
tasks.still_hard: The psychologist remains accountable for the report. A mandated form may still have to be typed by hand, and the report is health data.
tasks.human_edge: Only the psychologist can say what the findings mean and what the report must not claim.
tasks.altitude: The client meeting and the findings stay with the clinical psychologist. Less time goes to typing the first report. Decision rights do not move.

reach.task: Receive the findings a school is allowed to see
reach.learn: Which findings from the accepted report a school can receive

evidence.claim: Speech-driven reporting drafts clinical documentation from the clinician's own speech. A report draft here quotes stored notes rather than a new recording.
One psychiatry clinic tried ambient voice notes as a documentation assistant. This design does not use that study's minutes as a saving.
The psychologist stays accountable for an AI-drafted note or test report.
A client report can be drafted from the psychologist's own notes and stored scores. The psychologist still checks the findings. Model knowledge.

assumptions: Means priors sum to 100. Largest remainder gives screens 22, a three-point grid prior, mail 4, documents 45, and meetings 26. The grid points are folded into documents because the scores the report quotes already sit on the {OTHER} record. Documents are 12 to read, 20 to check, and 16 to commit. Screens are 8 to open and 14 to draft. That split is a design choice, not a measured study.

The draft reads chart notes and stored scores opened first, agreed facts from the client meeting, and the report headings. If a score is not a stored field, the draft omits it and the psychologist types the figure while checking. If the notes are not stored, the draft does not run.

The loop stops when the draft is written. It does not wait for a person. The check names accepted client report v1. The commit and the referrer send do not edit that version. A later edit voids the check.
The referrer is treated as outside the organisation. The client meeting stays at full time. This report draft does not repeat the session-note saving.
No focal upkeep is added. Exceptions sit inside the remaining check. Record runtime earns no labour saving.
unknowns: Whether the referrer is outside the organisation.
Whether the referrer requires a mandated form the psychologist must type by hand.
Whether the test scores are stored fields the report draft can quote.
research_questions: Which report headings does this referrer already require?

already_counted.description: Checking findings, limits, and the required paperwork is already the full time of that check.

incremental.description: Keeping the referrer's report headings available in the clinical record module.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low is 0 when a court or insurer form must be typed by hand. High is 8 when chart notes are stored but the psychologist still rewrites many findings. The client meeting, the check, the commit, and the referrer send stay at full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Sessions, harm judgements, and diagnoses stay with the clinical psychologist. First drafts of notes and reports take less typing. Decision rights do not move.
reach: School Psychologists: write a classroom observation a clinic note can cite without repeating the session.
Neuropsychologists: read a scaled score before choosing the next test.
skills_to_grow: Comparing a drafted note with what the patient said.
Keeping test item responses as stored fields so a norm table can be applied.
role.ambitious_version: This design stops at one accepted note and one accepted report for this encounter. It does not add a new clinical service.
